meta.title: Hire for an open role: requisition to signed contract
standards: Title VII of the Civil Rights Act
EEOC Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures (29 CFR Part 1607)
Immigration Reform and Control Act (IRCA) / Form I-9

overview.purpose: Take an approved hiring need from an open requisition through sourcing, structured selection, a conditional offer, compliant screening, and a fully executed employment agreement — consistently, defensibly, and with the candidate experience and legal obligations handled at every step.
scope_in: Job description and job-related selection criteria
Structured evaluation, selection, and reference checks
Conditional offer, FCRA-compliant background screening, and adverse action
Offer, negotiation, and execution of the employment agreement
Initiation of right-to-work (Form I-9) and handoff to onboarding
scope_out: Long-range workforce planning and headcount strategy
outcomes: A qualified candidate hired through a consistent, documented, defensible process
A fully executed employment agreement on file
Right-to-work verification initiated with a clean handoff to onboarding

definitions.ATS: Applicant Tracking System — the system of record for the requisition and candidates.
definitions.CRA: Consumer Reporting Agency — third party that produces the background report under the FCRA.
definitions.BARS: Behaviorally Anchored Rating Scale — defined behavior for each score on the interview scorecard.
definitions.Conditional offer: An offer contingent on clearing screening and right-to-work checks.
definitions.Adverse action: A decision not to hire based on a background report, triggering FCRA notices.
definitions.At-will: Employment either party may end at any time, subject to law and any contract terms.

assumptions: US-based W-2 employment is assumed; this is not legal advice.
Requirements vary by state and municipality (background checks, ban-the-box, pay transparency, contract vs at-will) — confirm local rules.
The employer uses an ATS and a third-party CRA for background screening.

roles.name: Hiring Manager
responsibilities: Owns the role, its requirements, and the final selection decision
Defines job-related criteria and participates in structured interviews

roles.name: Recruiter / Talent Acquisition
responsibilities: Drives the process end to end and owns the candidate experience
Sources, screens, coordinates interviews, and extends offers

roles.name: HR Business Partner
responsibilities: Oversees process compliance, recordkeeping, and offer/contract governance
Owns FCRA adverse action and right-to-work verification

roles.name: Interview Panel
responsibilities: Conducts structured interviews and completes anchored scorecards

roles.name: Compensation / Finance Approver
responsibilities: Approves headcount, budget, and the compensation package
Confirms the offer sits within the approved band

roles.name: Legal / Compliance
responsibilities: Reviews non-standard offer terms and the employment agreement
Advises on adverse action and jurisdictional requirements

roles.name: Candidate
responsibilities: External party; responds to the offer and completes required documents

skills: Working knowledge of EEOC, FCRA, and I-9 obligations
access: ATS with permission to create requisitions and post roles
materials: Interview scorecard templates with behavioral anchors (BARS)
Standalone FCRA disclosure and authorization document (single purpose)

safety.note: Evaluate every candidate for the same role against the same job-related criteria, in the same order; do not discriminate on protected characteristics.
Interviews, tests, and screens are selection procedures — keep them job-related and consistent with business necessity, and monitor adverse impact (4/5 rule).
safety.standard_ref: EEOC Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures (29 CFR Part 1607)

safety.note: Candidate and employee personal data must have a lawful basis, limited access, and defined retention; retain selection records at least one year (two years for federal contractors).

A background check via a CRA requires a standalone written disclosure and separate authorization; an adverse decision requires the two-step FCRA process (pre-adverse notice with the report and a Summary of Rights, a reasonable waiting period, then a final adverse-action notice).
Where fair-chance law applies, delay any criminal-history inquiry until after a conditional offer, and apply an EEOC individualized assessment (nature of the offense, time elapsed, job-relatedness).
Verify employment eligibility with Form I-9 — Section 1 no later than the first day of work, Section 2 within three business days of the start date; run E-Verify if enrolled.
Offer and honor reasonable accommodations to candidates with disabilities throughout the process.

steps.title: Open and document the requisition
steps.description: Capture the confirmed hiring need as a requisition in the ATS: role, level, reporting line, justification, target start, and the business case. This is the record everything else hangs off.
steps.verification: A requisition record exists in the ATS with role, level, reporting line, and business case.
steps.notes: Keep the business case job-related; it anchors the selection criteria.

steps.title: Approve headcount and budget
steps.description: Finance / compensation reviews the requisition against headcount plan and budget and either approves it to open or returns it. No sourcing happens before approval.
steps.verification: The requisition shows an approval record with approver, date, and budgeted band.
steps.escalation: If budget is contested, escalate to the department head and HRBP.

steps.title: Finalize the job description and selection criteria
steps.description: With the hiring manager, turn the requisition into an approved job description and a structured scorecard: 6–12 job-related competencies, each with behavioral anchors. Requirements must be necessary for the role.
steps.verification: Every listed requirement is job-related and consistent with business necessity; the scorecard defines competencies with behavioral anchors.

guardrails: Avoid criteria that exclude protected groups without business necessity.

steps.title: Source candidates
steps.description: Post the role to the required internal and external channels and run sourcing and referrals to build a diverse, qualified pipeline. Honor any internal-posting or pay-transparency requirements.
steps.verification: The role is posted to all required channels and a candidate pipeline is building in the ATS.
steps.notes: Include the pay range where pay-transparency law requires it.

steps.title: Screen applications
steps.description: Review applicants against the same job-related criteria and shortlist. Do not ask about criminal history at this stage where fair-chance law applies.
steps.verification: All applicants are screened against the same criteria and screening decisions are logged.

guardrails: Do not ask about criminal history on the application (ban-the-box / fair-chance).
Screen every applicant against the same job-related criteria and log decisions.

steps.title: Recruiter phone screen
steps.description: Hold a consistent phone/video screen with each shortlisted candidate to confirm fit, motivation, logistics, and compensation expectations.
steps.verification: Each candidate is screened with the same core questions; notes are recorded in the ATS.

steps.title: Administer job-related assessments
steps.description: Where the role calls for it, administer the same validated, job-related assessment to every candidate and record results. Skip only if no assessment is used for this role.
steps.verification: The same assessment is sent to all candidates for the role and results are recorded.

guardrails: Use a validated, job-related assessment applied identically to all candidates.

steps.title: Conduct structured interviews
steps.description: Run structured panel interviews using the same core questions for every candidate, scoring against the BARS scorecard. Offer reasonable accommodations on request.
steps.verification: Every interviewer completes an anchored scorecard with evidence notes; the same core questions were used.
steps.escalation: Accommodation requests go to the HRBP for prompt handling.

guardrails: Ask all candidates the same core questions; score against the anchors.

steps.title: Debrief and make the selection decision
steps.description: Convene a structured debrief to reconcile scores against the anchors — not to reach consensus by social pressure — and make a documented, job-related decision. Retain the records.
steps.verification: The decision and its rationale are documented and stored; the selection-rate is checked against the 4/5 rule.

steps.title: Complete reference checks
steps.description: Run consistent, job-related reference checks on the selected candidate and record the results before making the offer conditional.
steps.verification: References are completed with consistent questions and results are recorded.

steps.title: Approve compensation and extend a conditional verbal offer
steps.description: Confirm the package is approved and within band, then extend a verbal offer that is explicitly conditional on clearing screening and right-to-work checks. Follow up in writing summarizing the key terms.
steps.verification: Compensation is approved and within band; the conditional verbal offer and its terms are confirmed by email.
steps.escalation: Out-of-band compensation requires comp_approver sign-off before the offer is extended.

steps.title: Candidate response and negotiation
steps.description: The candidate accepts, negotiates, or declines the conditional offer. Route accordingly; re-approve compensation for any counter-offer.
steps.verification: The candidate's response is recorded; any negotiated changes are captured before proceeding.

steps.title: Disclose, authorize, and run the background check
steps.description: Provide the standalone FCRA disclosure and obtain separate written authorization, then order the background check via the CRA. Keep the conditional offer in place while screening runs.
steps.verification: A signed standalone disclosure and authorization are on file before the report is ordered; the report is stored securely.

guardrails: Never order the report before a signed standalone disclosure and authorization are on file.
The disclosure must be a single-purpose document, not embedded in the application.
Store background data securely with access limited to need-to-know.

steps.title: Adjudicate the results
steps.description: Review the background and reference results. If nothing disqualifying is found, proceed to the written offer. If there is potentially disqualifying information, apply an individualized assessment and enter adverse action.
steps.verification: The adjudication applies job-relatedness and an individualized assessment; the rationale is documented.

steps.title: Run FCRA adverse action (only if withdrawing)
steps.description: Send the pre-adverse-action notice with a copy of the report and the Summary of Rights, wait a reasonable period for dispute (best practice at least five business days; some jurisdictions longer), then either restore the offer or send the final adverse-action notice.
steps.verification: Both notices are documented with dates and the waiting period is observed; no irreversible internal action is taken during the waiting period.
steps.escalation: Legal reviews any contested or borderline adverse action before the final notice.

branches.condition: Dispute resolved in the candidate's favor or record corrected
Adverse action upheld — offer rescinded, revisit the shortlist

guardrails: Do not mark the candidate rejected or backfill the role during the waiting period.

steps.title: Extend the formal written offer
steps.description: Issue the written offer letter / employment agreement matching the approved compensation and the verbal terms, with an acceptance deadline. Route any non-standard terms to Legal first.
steps.verification: The sent offer matches approved terms; non-standard terms were reviewed by Legal; an acceptance deadline is set.

guardrails: The offer letter must match the approved compensation and the verbal offer.
Route non-standard terms (equity, severance, non-compete) to Legal before sending.

steps.title: Countersign and execute the agreement
steps.description: On candidate signature, countersign to fully execute the employment agreement and confirm the start date. This is the signed contract that completes the hire.
steps.verification: Candidate signature and employer countersignature are on file; the start date is confirmed.

steps.title: Initiate right-to-work and hand off to onboarding
steps.description: Start Form I-9 and (if enrolled) E-Verify, and hand the new hire to onboarding. Section 1 is due no later than the first day; Section 2 within three business days of the start date.
steps.verification: Form I-9 is initiated and the onboarding handoff package is delivered to the onboarding owner.

guardrails: Section 1 no later than the first day; Section 2 within three business days of start.
Do not use I-9 to pre-screen work authorization before offer acceptance.
Never open a duplicate E-Verify case for the same employee.

steps.notes: I-9 Section 2 and day-one tasks complete in onboarding (SOP-HR-001).

references: EEOC — Background Checks: What Employers Need to Know (eeoc.gov)
EEOC Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures, 29 CFR Part 1607
FTC/CFPB — A Summary of Your Rights Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act
USCIS — Form I-9, Employment Eligibility Verification (uscis.gov/i-9)
